judge_assessment.explanation: I redid all ten divisions and every one matches the key: (7+2i)(7-2i) = 53; (6+4i)/2i = 2-3i; (5+5i)/(2+i) = 3+i; (11+10i)/(4-i) = 2+3i; Z = (2+23i)/(3+2i) = 4+5i ohms; (11-10i)/(3+2i) = 1-4i; (9-6i)/3i = -2-3i; 25/(3+4i) = 3-4i; I = (1+8i)/(2+i) = 2+3i amps; and in problem 10, x = (4+7i)/(3+2i) = 2+i and the zero of (1-i)x-(6+2i) is 2+4i. The judge's ACCEPT is right on the mathematics. Its implicit "nothing needs manual review" is not: the run recorded zero manual items (gate_log manual flags false) while three problems print written asks - problem 6 "Say in one sentence why that method does not work here", problem 8 "State what the denominator times its conjugate equals before you simplify", and problem 10's closing "say which conjugate you multiplied by in part (b) and why". Problem 8's asked-for statement (25) is also a machine-checkable value the verify JSON never declares - verify.json id 8 holds only the quotient - so the printed request has no coverage of either kind.

strengths_to_preserve: The circuit thread is real physics, not decoration: problem 5 recovers impedance from V = IZ and problem 9 recovers current from the same law, with "ohms" and "amps" declared as answer_unit, printed on the sheet's \answerline, and boxed in the key - and the key closes problem 5 by checking (4+5i)(3+2i) = 2+23i volts.

Problem 8 (25/(3+4i)) is chosen so that a^2+b^2 equals the numerator, which is why the key can end with "the scaling was exactly 1" - a structural observation the student can reuse rather than an arithmetic result.

The two declared traps are the two real failure modes of this skill: 45 from treating i^2 as +1 in the conjugate product, and the 1/i = i sign flip on problem 2; the key prints both as grading notes tied to the exact wrong value.

The ramp is genuinely graded by divisor type - pure imaginary (2, 7), binomial (3, 4, 8), applied (5, 9), misconception (6) and equations in disguise (10) - so the method choice is exercised without repeating a template ten times.

root_causes.description: A sheet routed as machine_first recorded no manual items at all, so the one-sentence explanations attached to otherwise checkable problems were left with no reviewer, contradicting the prompt's instruction to label genuinely open responses.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 6 asks "Say in one sentence why that method does not work here"; verify.json id 6 holds a single `eval` entry.
worksheet.tex problem 10 ends "In one sentence, say which conjugate you multiplied by in part (b) and why"; verify.json id 10 holds a `solve` and a `zeros` entry only.
The machine observation records gate_chain_manual_flags = false and gate_log.txt reports 0 manual across the run.

root_causes.description: A value the stem explicitly asks the student to STATE was treated as an intermediate step rather than as a printed response.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 8 says "State what the denominator times its conjugate equals before you simplify"; the answer (25) is checkable but verify.json id 8 declares only the quotient 3-4i.
The key does print it ("First the requested statement: (3+4i)(3-4i) = 9+16 = 25"), so the key is ahead of the verification data.

improvements.title: Record every explanation, diagnosis and named-error item as a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat an item that asks the student to explain, justify, describe, name the wrong move, or draw/mark a representation as a MANUAL response even when a numeric part of the same problem is machine-checkable. SKILL.md and references/manual-review-aid.md should state the rule, and the response-coverage gate should scan each problem segment for imperative prose asks (Explain, Describe, Say why, Which ... did, State how, Sketch, Draw and label) and fail when the problem carries no `manual` entry. Here problems 6, 8 and 10 each print a one-sentence ask on a sheet that recorded zero manual items.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem stem containing "Explain what went wrong" and a verify id holding only `eval` entries must make the gate exit non-zero; adding a `manual` entry for that problem must make it exit 0. The fixture passes every gate today, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review list delivered in final_response.md becomes true, and graders stop treating an unreviewed explanation as machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will flag scaffolding prose that is not a graded ask ("Explain to yourself why..."), so the rule needs an explicit opt-out and a short allowlist to avoid pushing authors toward manual-everything.

improvements.title: Verify (or flag manual for) every response slot the worksheet prints
improvements.proposed_change: Make the verify JSON an inventory of PRINTED RESPONSES, not of terminal answers. SKILL.md should require one verify entry per answer location a problem prints (\ansblank, \ansline, \answerline, an \underline writing rule, or a table cell the student fills), with `manual` used where the response is not a value. Enforce it with a new gate wired into scripts/build.sh that segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.segment_spans, counts the answer-location macros and fill-in rules per problem, and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries for the same problem id. Here problem 8's explicitly requested statement (25) needs its own verify entry alongside the quotient.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem prints five \ansblank slots against a verify id carrying four entries must make the new gate exit non-zero; adding the missing entry (or a `manual` entry) must make it exit 0. Today no gate compares slot count with entry count, so the fixture passes the whole chain - the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant systemic gap in this run: a sheet can no longer claim complete verification while printing blanks nothing checked, and the answer key's Quick Answers bank stops shipping short rows.
improvements.risk: Sheets that use several blanks to scaffold ONE value ("x-coordinate: __ y-coordinate: __ so P' = (__, __)") will need either a coarser blank layout or a documented per-value grouping, so the gate needs a same-value exemption to avoid false failures.

case_summary: Accurate, application-driven complex-division practice: ten correct divisions, units declared and bound in both directions, two well-chosen traps, and a key that verifies each result by multiplying back. The gap is narrow but real - the sheet asks for three short written justifications and one explicitly stated intermediate value, and the run declares zero manual items and no entry for that value, so the packet reports complete coverage of responses it does not cover.
